items.definition:
a pole with a flat blade, used to propel a boat
He dipped the oar into the water and pulled.

a long-handled tool with two or three long, thick, pointed prongs, used for lifting and tossing hay
The farmer used a pitchfork to move the hay.

a unit of liquid capacity equal to a quarter of a gallon or two pints
I bought a quart of milk from the store.

a grain-like crop grown primarily for its edible seeds
Quinoa is a healthy alternative to rice or pasta.

a light snack or drink
Light refreshments will be served after the meeting.

The quality of being sharp
The chef tested the sharpness of the knife.

A card game played by one person; a single gem set alone
She spent the afternoon playing solitaire on her computer.

A plug of soft material inserted into a bodily cavity or wound to absorb fluid
She needed to buy tampons from the pharmacy.

a small four-stringed guitar-like instrument
She learned to play the ukulele during the lockdown.

a person employed to guard a building or property
The watchman patrols the building at night.

a feeling of great surprise or wonder
To her amazement, she won the lottery.

the hollow under the arm
He felt a tickle in his armpit.

an object or design carved from wood or stone
The museum displayed an ancient wooden carving.

academic work
Students must complete all coursework to pass the class.

a small ball of dough
I love eating chicken and dumplings.

a bird, especially a domestic one
Chickens and ducks are types of domestic fowl.

a small brown spot on the skin
She has many freckles on her nose.

a long-winged, web-footed seabird with a raucous call
A white gull flew over the ocean waves.

a small open-fronted hut or cubicle from which newspapers, refreshments, tickets, etc., are sold
We bought a map at the tourist kiosk.

a leguminous plant of the pea family, grown for its edible seeds
Lentil soup is a healthy and hearty meal.

a hammer with a large wooden head
He used a rubber mallet to tap the pieces into place.

the sound a cat makes
We heard a soft mew from the kitten.

a period when a country is not at war
During peacetime, the economy often thrives.

a system of physical exercises
She does Pilates twice a week for core strength.

a track or course for racing, especially horse racing
They spent the afternoon at the racecourse watching the horses.

water that has fallen as rain
We collected rainwater in a barrel for the garden.

a mobile device with a touchscreen display, designed to be worn on the wrist
He received a new smartwatch for his birthday.

the state or quality of being sore; pain or tenderness
He felt a slight soreness in his muscles after the workout.

A marine invertebrate with a star-shaped body.
We saw a beautiful starfish clinging to the rock.

A high-performance sports car.
He dreams of owning a bright red supercar one day.

Pliable twigs, typically willow, plaited or woven to make furniture or baskets.
We have a set of wicker chairs on our patio.

a close-fitting cap, often made of wool
He wore a warm beanie in the cold weather.

a training hall for martial arts
They practice karate every evening at the dojo.

a soft quilt filled with down, feathers, or a synthetic fiber, used as a bed covering
I bought a new duvet for my bed.

a small statue or statuette
She collects small porcelain figurines.

a small handbill or leaflet; a person or thing that flies
They handed out fliers for the concert.

a path for walking
We followed the narrow footpath through the woods.

a deep pan or appliance for frying food
She bought a new air fryer for healthier cooking.

Fluffy bits of fiber and fabric.
I need to clean the lint trap in the dryer.

An area of land that is low in elevation.
The lowlands are often fertile for farming.

A trough or open box in a stable or cowshed, from which horses or cattle feed.
The baby Jesus was laid in a manger.

A cosmetic treatment of the hands and fingernails.
She went to the salon for a manicure.

A cosmetic preparation used to moisturize the skin.
She applies moisturizer to her face every morning.

soft, pulpy mass
The overcooked vegetables turned into mush.

a person or machine that picks something
The fruit picker carefully selected the ripe apples.

a type of dog bred to retrieve game
Our golden retriever loves to play fetch in the park.

partially melted snow or ice
The streets were covered in dirty slush after the snowstorm.

the quality of being soft
She enjoyed the softness of the freshly laundered towels.

a rapidly rotating mass of water
The boat was caught in a strong whirlpool.

a long stiff hair growing from the snout or other part of the face of an animal
The cat twitched its whiskers.

a list of desired items
I've added a new laptop to my Christmas wishlist.

a breed of sheepdog
The loyal collie herded the sheep back to the pen.

a series of pleasant thoughts that distract one's attention from the present
She often loses herself in a daydream during boring meetings.

a bubbling or hissing sound; effervescence
The soda lost its fizz after sitting out for too long.

a breakfast and snack food consisting of rolled oats, nuts, honey, etc.
She eats granola with yogurt every morning for a healthy breakfast.

a car with a door at the back that opens upwards, often including the rear window
She prefers driving a hatchback because it's easy to park and has good cargo space.

the state of being impatient
Her impatience grew as she waited for the bus.

the act of treating someone or something badly
The animals suffered from severe mistreatment at the shelter.

a type of coffee made with chocolate syrup or powder
I'd like a hot mocha with whipped cream, please.

a smooth, oily preparation rubbed on the skin for medicinal purposes
Apply the ointment to the affected area twice a day.

a substance or tool that removes something
I need some stain remover for this shirt.

a mythical figure who brings sleep and pleasant dreams
The children were tired and ready for the Sandman to visit.

a short, light sleep or nap
I hit the snooze button on my alarm clock.

a sheet of waterproof material
We covered the firewood with a tarp to keep it dry.
